messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]
Age: 12
Sex: Female
Date of Admission: [redacted]
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the emergency room with intense left flank pain, which was discovered to be caused by an obstructing calculus in the left ureter and nephrolithiasis. The patient was treated with pain control medications and hydration, and subsequently referred to a nephrologist. The patient underwent a "stone risk study" and renal ultrasound, which showed multiple bilateral cysts and renal calculi. Genetic testing was performed and identified dual mutations in GANAB and PKD1genes. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Instructions:
-The patient should follow up with the nephrologist for further evaluation and management of the polycystic kidney disease.
-The patient should return if she experiences any further pain or symptoms.

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with the nephrologist for further evaluation and management of the polycystic kidney disease.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The presenting problem was left flank pain from an obstructing calculus in the left ureter, with nephrolithiasis. That points to N20 (calculus of kidney and ureter). Polycystic kidney disease (Q61) is also present, and it is the underlying condition. The principal diagnosis is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. Here the admission was for the obstructing ureteric stone, and the cystic disease was identified during the workup afterwards.

The discharge instructions emphasise follow-up of the polycystic kidney disease. The stone episode was still the reason for the emergency presentation and treatment, so I chose N20.

**N20**
